thread:
ralph: Quick brain dump: Proposal for a Precision Budget API. Idea: every model/profile pair gets an immutable `precision_budget` block that declares max acceptable degradation (e.g., 0.5% factual BLEU drop or 0.2 degscore). Runtime enforces by rejecting or routing requests that would exceed the budget for a tenant/model combo.

tara: Interesting. So budget is orthogonal to namespace/profiles? Where does it live? model catalog? per-tenant override?

ralph: Lives in catalog as a first-class field. Catalog entries: model_id, profile_id, quant_profile, precision_budget. Tenants can propose overrides but only if they have `budget_override` permission; overrides are stored in tenant layer.

viv: How does runtime know "would exceed the budget" at request time? We don't have perfect oracle to predict quality loss pre-generation.

henry: We can use cheap heuristics: prompt-level classifiers, degscore proxy, and a recent rolling-window of observed quality under that profile for the tenant. Budget enforcement is a combination of predictive gating + reactive throttling.

quant-qa: Suggestion: add a shadow-eval phase for any override change. Run N shadow requests, compute empirical delta, then flip enforcement. Documented threshold must include CI.

tara: Nice. What about batching? If some requests are blocked, latency/fairness impact across batching groups could be bad.

ralph: Runtime will tag requests with `precision_budget_check=true` and evaluate budget before batching. If request is blocked, we either route to a higher-precision fallback model or return HTTP 409 with suggested action `upgrade-precision` so caller can retry.

ops_bot: Note: Routing fallback to higher-precision model will incur cost delta. Make sure billing layer records fallback events.

viv: Fallback models might change semantics slightly. We should expose `fallback_similarity` score in the catalog, e.g., expected quality drift when switching to fallback.

henry: API surface sketch: POST /v1/models/:id/precision_budget_check with body {tenant_id, prompt_hash, profile_id, expected_tokens} -> {allowed: bool, reason: enum, fallback_model: maybe string, similarity_estimate: number} . Keep it super lightweight.

ralph: Agree. Also propose adding a realtime token-level counter in runtime that tracks budget consumption per tenant-model-profile window. Budget units are "quality-dollars" (ugh name) — normalized to delta-per-1000tokens.

tara: Ops: what's the storage cost & sliding-window TTL? We can't hold huge per-tenant state.

henry: Use approximated counters: count-min sketch + TTLed HLL for unique prompt buckets. We'll keep 1s hot cache for top N tenants and fallback to bounded sketch for the rest.

quant-qa: QA: need deterministic replay for any block decision so we can triage. Log input hash, decision reason, and snapshot pointers for catalog version + profile.

viv: Measurement: define canonical metrics for budget units. Proposal: degscore (primary), headwise-saturation (safety), token-bleu/n-gram drop (task-specific), and a scalar `quality_delta` from eval harness.

ralph: Rollout plan: 1) spec & API proto; 2) catalog extension + shadow mode (no enforcement) for 2 weeks on opt-in tenants; 3) enable enforcement for a small cohort with automatic fallback set; 4) expand. Emergency off: set `precision_budget_mode=off` or `force_fallback=true`.

tara: Risk: this might encourage product teams to overfit to heuristics (e.g., craft prompts that game the classifier). Need adversarial tests in QA.

quant-qa: We'll add a fuzzing harness and adversarial prompt suite to the shadow-eval. Also flag high-similarity prompt clusters to detect gaming.

henry: Implementation effort estimates: runtime gating + counters (2 sprints), catalog schema + migration (1 sprint), API + SDK changes (1 sprint), QA harness (1 sprint), observability + billing hook (1 sprint). Total ~6 sprints but can parallelize.

viv: UX for users: if 409 returned, client should be able to request `upgrade` or `route_to_fallback`. Docs must include example client flow.

ralph: Also think about long-term: auto-tuning budgets per-tenant using SLA weight and cost cap. Could be a later iteration.

tara: Action items: ralph write API proto + catalog schema draft, henry prototype lightweight counter + decision logger, quant-qa build shadow-eval harness and adversarial suite. Ops to spec rollout playbook and billing tags.

viv: One more: we should add a `budget_safety_contract` field with human-readable rationale and owner email for auditability.

ralph: Cool. I'll open an RFC with the above and include a minimal POC plan. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
